claims.text: Elevated-temperature brittle behavior in the proposed SLM-fabricated HEA is governed by grain-boundary morphology rather than grain-boundary segregation or deleterious intermetallic precipitation.
Straight grain boundaries are susceptible to localized strain concentration at triple junctions.
Strain localization at straight-boundary triple junctions promotes intergranular cracking and hot ductility loss.
Serrated grain boundaries distribute deformation strain more uniformly than straight grain boundaries.
Serrated grain boundaries retard crack nucleation, microcrack connection, and crack propagation.
The initial material is an SLM-fabricated, single-phase HEA with primarily straight grain boundaries.
Reducing the cooling rate after solution heat treatment permits coarsening of L12-structured gamma-prime precipitates.
Coarsened gamma-prime precipitates interact with mobile grain boundaries and induce a serrated grain-boundary morphology.
Tensile and creep loading at 650 degrees Celsius can reveal the proposed hot-ductility and creep-rupture effects.
A temperature of approximately 650 degrees Celsius is representative of the intended service conditions.
The straight-boundary baseline undergoes brittle intergranular fracture and a rapid ductility drop at elevated temperature.
At 650 degrees Celsius, serrated-boundary material will have approximately 3.5 times the tensile fracture strain of the straight-boundary baseline.
At 650 degrees Celsius, serrated-boundary material can have creep rupture life up to 400 times that of the straight-boundary baseline.
Serrated boundaries will show lower local strain concentration at triple junctions than straight boundaries.
The proposed mechanism may cease to govern if significant grain-boundary segregation or deleterious secondary-phase formation occurs.
Oxidizing environments may alter the operative deformation and embrittlement mechanisms.
The exact ductility and creep-life multipliers depend on alloy composition, processing details, and test conditions.

contradictions.description: The scope is described as applying to single-phase HEAs, but the intervention explicitly relies on coarsening L12 gamma-prime precipitates, making the treated comparison state precipitate-containing rather than strictly single-phase. This is reconcilable only if 'single-phase' refers exclusively to the initial state.
